description: NixOS, Home Manager, Hyprland and the boundaries between reproducible packages and personal state.
text:
Start with the source NixOS configuration repository · Published Neovim configuration The public NixOS repository is the published baseline. The local security maintenance verified on 16 October has not yet been committed to that repository. The interactive guide uses short, explanatory examples; it is not a copy of private machine state.
Two configuration layers The flake pins Nixpkgs, Home Manager and Fenix. NixOS declares system packages, hardware integration and services. Home Manager declares user packages and configuration links. The system build integrates both layers, so package/configuration changes can be reviewed together.
flake.lock records exact input revisions. A pinned build still needs compatible hardware, application data and separately restored credentials.
A keyboard-first desktop Hyprland runs the Wayland desktop, with XWayland available for applications that need it. SDDM handles login; Kitty provides the terminal, Waybar the status bar, and Rofi the launcher. PipeWire and WirePlumber provide audio and media routing.
Configured desktop shortcuts include Super + Return for the terminal, Super + B for the browser, Super + Space for the launcher and Super + O for file search. These are configuration examples rather than browser shortcuts.
Intel graphics drive the laptop display. NVIDIA is available through explicit offload. This separation keeps ordinary desktop work on the integrated GPU while allowing a compatible task to request the dedicated GPU.
Packages and mutable state Nix supplies Neovim and its language servers. Personal Lua configuration comes from a separate live Neovim checkout. Application data, working trees, browser profiles, credentials and databases are separate state; they are not recreated by a package build.
Secrets belong outside public source and outside unfiltered flake sources. Git ignoring a file does not protect it from every other tool that copies a directory.
What was actually checked On 16 October, the prepared security configuration passed a full NixOS build and was activated successfully. Both Home Manager activations succeeded. System DNS resolved a real domain, NVIDIA-offloaded OpenGL reported the MX350 renderer, and Hyprland reported no configuration errors. Both storage drives passed fresh short self-tests. These are dated observations, not a guarantee about every future workload.
Read build and verification for the maintenance sequence and remaining boundaries, or return to the interactive Workbench .
title: How the environment fits together

description: A practical route through the editor, private notes, links and graph.
text:
Try it without an account Open the public editor to try Markdown, preview and optional Vim. The scratchpad lives in the tab; this example does not save it to a private account. Download anything you want to keep before leaving.
Explore the public graph for an original six-note sample. It does not read private notes or start a processing job.
Create a private workspace Open the hosted workspace , register using the displayed requirements and keep the private recovery key securely. Recovery is based on your passphrase/key; no email reset service is connected. Keep the recovery key out of messages and screenshots.
Create notes or checklists, set labels/colors, pin useful items and use search. Save a note before relying on it being persisted. Archives and trash are distinct; permanently deleted content cannot be recovered through the normal UI. Account export and deletion are available.
Write and preview Use standard editing, Markdown preview or split view. Optional Vim uses the editor’s Vim mode; it does not embed a shell or run arbitrary Neovim plugins. A plain-text fallback remains available if the rich editor fails to load.
Formatting, find/replace, in-tab undo/redo and explicit save controls are described in the editor manual . Markdown downloads preserve the note text. Raw HTML and automatically loaded remote images are restricted in preview.
A save failure is not success: keep the draft, read the error and retry. Conflicting revisions require deliberate resolution. In-tab history and dirty-navigation prompts are useful safeguards, not crash-proof or offline storage.
Connect the work Insert a stable link using the note picker, or use a title link such as [[Project plan]]. Stable links retain the note’s identity when its title changes. Duplicate titles are ambiguous; missing or unavailable targets are shown explicitly instead of silently choosing another note.
Open a note’s outgoing references and backlinks, or use the graph’s title/label/archive filters and focused neighborhood. The graph also has a keyboard-accessible HTML list. For supported syntax, rename/deletion behavior and all controls, read connections .
Bounds and recovery The free preview is capped at 100 accounts and, per account, 250 notes, 50 labels and 2 MiB of note text. Graph drawing is bounded to 500 nodes/1,000 edges, with at most 256 scanned references per note. These are configured limits, not proof of capacity at every load.
Do not treat this as end-to-end encrypted, collaborative or continuously synchronized between tabs. There is no paid checkout, durable revision archive or Pageweft/Sonaweft importer yet. Export important work and report unclear behavior to support .
title: Using Noteweld

description: Inspect a PDF, choose a conversion method, review the source and keep portable files.
text:
See a completed result Open Pageweft or explore the original PDF/Markdown/ZIP example linked from its website and the portfolio. Viewing the completed example does not run a GPU conversion.
Inspect before processing Upload a PDF you have permission to process. Each file can be at most 64 MiB and 1,000 PDF pages; up to five files can be inspected, with each conversion confirmed separately. Choose the original PDF page numbers or ranges and review the text-layer inspection and quote.
Inspection does not establish that OCR will preserve every formula, table or symbol. Encrypted, malformed or resource-heavy documents can be rejected. Keep the original.
Choose the extraction route Automatic MinerU: use the supported text/OCR decision path and structured extraction. Forced OCR: request OCR explicitly where the text layer is unsuitable. Text-only: use the cheaper CPU route for available text; it does not provide OCR, extracted images or full layout reconstruction. The small public trial processes one selected page, subject to the remaining session/IP/global allowance. Full funded processing is implemented but unavailable while commercial checkout is closed. Do not assume that seeing a tariff means a live purchase is possible.
Follow work and handle failures Selected pages are divided into bounded sections. Successful sections remain available if another section fails. Inspect the status before retrying; an uncertain request should not be repeated as a new billable job.
Use explicit retry or selected-page reprocessing with its displayed quote. Cancelling queued work and cancelling an already running section have different settlement behavior. The conversion release documents those rules.
Review against the source Use original-PDF page references, reported symptoms and the corrections editor. Corrections remain separate from original engine output; revision checks help prevent stale edits. Detection flags cover specific symptoms and cannot guarantee that unflagged text is correct.
Choose single-document, per-page, page-group or PDF-bookmark exports. The ZIP can carry relative image paths, a manifest, source metadata, original engine output and an optional source PDF. Keep raw output when investigating extraction defects.
Keep your files and recovery key Download results before the 48-hour retention window expires; scheduled cleanup removes expired source/output files. Saved financial/recovery records are separate from file retention. Retain the private recovery key securely and use deletion/discard controls when appropriate.
Current pricing and boundaries are in the technical overview . Owner deployment and incident procedures are in operations . Paddle approval and real payment verification are still required; no earnings or perfect OCR is promised.
title: Using Pageweft

description: Go from an authorized recording to a timestamped transcript and portable source-linked notes.
text:
Hear a completed example Open the original example to hear source audio, inspect the actual recognition/review and download a hashed bundle. This precomputed example does not start another transcription job.
Upload and inspect The hosted workflow accepts authorized English audio/video up to 64 MiB and 60 minutes. Upload a file and inspect its duration/quote before confirming work. The hosted application does not download arbitrary platform URLs or use your browser cookies.
An available free sample processes the first 30 seconds, transcription only. It is once per workspace/IP hash and subject to small global and admission quotas. Paid processing packs remain closed while Paddle approval and actual payment tests are outstanding.
Decide whether to use AI review Review is optional and requires consent to send transcript text to DeepSeek. Source audio is not sent to that text provider. Standard/advanced review choices have different quoted service tariffs; current values are in the technical overview .
Original recognition, user corrections, generated notes and separately sourced research remain different artifacts. A generated summary or scholarly metadata match does not certify that a claim is true.
Listen, correct and export Open timestamped segments, listen to the corresponding source and search the text. Save corrections as a separate revision; the original recognition remains available. Conflicts or failed saves need resolution before you rely on the edit.
Export original Markdown/text/JSON/SRT/VTT, corrected Markdown/JSON and optional notes/research questions. The versioned instascript-export/v1 bundle includes identity, timing, provenance and hashes. Producing that bundle does not yet implement a Noteweld importer.
Failed selected processing releases its reservation; an explicit retry gets a fresh quote and may reuse retained recognition. Do not blindly create a second job after an uncertain response.
Local CLI and retention The standalone CLI also supports authorized URLs through its own local tools. Local model downloads, platform access and optional provider charges are separate from the hosted service. Follow the CLI setup , not the archived agent/demo scripts.
Hosted source/results expire after 48 hours and are removed by scheduled cleanup. Download outputs while retained. There is no immediate self-service delete control yet; use support with ownership proof without sending recordings or recovery keys. No diarization, speaker identification or certified transcription is claimed.
title: Using Sonaweft

description: Understand the separate browser-only demonstration and its storage boundary.
text:
Open the portfolio demo Open the bundled demo or launch it from the portfolio’s vanilla JavaScript card. This is a separate implementation from Noteweld. It demonstrates native browser APIs rather than the professional Next.js application.
Work in one browser Try notes and checklists, pin/color/label controls, archive and trash. Storage belongs to this browser and website origin. It does not create a cloud account, synchronize devices or inherit Noteweld’s editor/graph features.
Use a disposable test note when exploring the demo. Browser data clearing, private browsing, storage limits or a different origin can affect persistence. Keep important content outside a portfolio demonstration.
Save, search and recover Use either search field to find titles, bodies, labels or checklist text. Create a text note or checklist; labels imported in a JSON backup are available in navigation immediately. Use the edit button or open a card; Escape saves and returns focus.
Export a JSON backup before clearing browser storage. Imports validate the file and merge without replacing existing note IDs. When a save fails, the app shows an error and retains an open draft for retry. Malformed existing data opens a recovery screen with a raw JSON download instead of reseeding the database.
Archive keeps a note available for later. Delete from Archive moves it to Trash. Restore recovers it; Delete forever and Empty Trash ask for confirmation. There is no automatic seven-day deletion.
Release boundary The published portfolio bundle is refreshed from the same production build as the standalone demo. The source release records 14 unit tests, 22 Chromium journeys, four viewport widths and no automated WCAG A/AA findings on the tested seeded screens. These checks do not certify every browser or replace usability testing.
Reminders and inactive settings controls are omitted. The professional Noteweld editor, Vim mode, graph, cloud accounts and payments are separate. Read the implementation guide and release history for the exact boundary.

description: CPU web hosting, on-demand workers and the costs that remain after compute stops.
text:
More than a GPU rental Modal runs application containers on CPU as well as GPU resources. It supports HTTP applications, background functions, schedules, persistent volumes and secrets. An HTTP server can be Python/FastAPI or a Node process; the deployment wrapper does not require every application to be written in Python.
Official references: HTTP applications , autoscaling , persistent volumes and secrets . Checked on 16 October 2026; provider policies and prices can change.
The current deployment Component Hosting Persistent state Portfolio, vanilla demo and this Hugo library GitHub Pages Static versioned files; vanilla demo uses browser storage Pageweft web/API and extraction jobs Modal CPU containers and A10G workers Separate document and serialized SQLite ledger volumes Sonaweft web/API, speech and review coordination Modal CPU containers and L4 workers Separate media, model-cache and serialized SQLite ledger volumes Noteweld web/API Modal Node/Next.js CPU container Isolated Neon PostgreSQL; encrypted backups in Modal Paddle handles commercial payments rather than hosting these websites. DeepSeek is an optional text-inference provider for Sonaweft. No shared customer wallet or login is implemented. Linguavell is a separate startup project.
Why this choice fits the previews Pageweft already had working MinerU execution on Modal. Reusing that provider allowed a small CPU web process to dispatch bounded expensive extraction separately. Sonaweft fits the same pattern with speech workers. Noteweld can run as a standard Node server, retaining portable PostgreSQL access rather than requiring another web-host account.
Containers can shut down after inactivity. The laptop is only a development/deployment client and does not need to remain online for the hosted applications to work. The Hugo blog is static and adds no application server or paid API.
The tradeoffs A request after inactivity can wait for a cold start. Keeping containers warm improves responsiveness but increases cost. Retained files, cached models, scheduled cleanup, database storage, backups and network usage can still consume resources when no customer job runs. Scale-to-zero compute is not a universal zero-bill promise.
Current container/concurrency caps deliberately constrain the previews. They are not a measured promise for thousands of simultaneous users. Internal admission allowances are distinct from a provider-wide spending limit. External automatic alerts and a saved global hard spending cap are not established by these releases.
Portability and review Noteweld uses a Node application and standard PostgreSQL driver; it can move to another suitable container/PostgreSQL host with configuration and deployment work. The Python applications keep processing logic separate from Modal wrappers, but function dispatch, volumes and scheduling are real provider dependencies. Migration would require replacing those integrations and validating storage/ledger semantics.
The current arrangement is an economical starting point to measure. Actual invoices, customer workload and cold-start tolerance should guide later hosting changes. It does not establish that Modal will be the cheapest host at every future traffic level.

description: The implementation sequence, successful commands, deployment prerequisites and recorded corrections.
text:
Start from the evidence The current source is connected-notes handoff f6901ff . Application code for that collection is e1b8740; earlier foundations are not descriptions of every current feature. Read the usage guide before following the implementation record.
1. Repair account and note persistence The early registration work validated identity/password input, seeded accounts and preserved failed form input. The then-selected Neon HTTP adapter supported a batch operation rather than interactive transaction callbacks. Its mocked-transport checks were explicitly not evidence of database rollback.
The reliability foundation switched to standard pg/Drizzle transactions shared between local PostgreSQL and Neon. It added real seed rollback/races, per-account ownership, note revisions/idempotency, trash rules and label consistency. A new database and restricted runtime role were provisioned for the preview; the original Keep database was not migrated. The private provisioning values are deliberately absent from this library.
Recovery-key hashing, session revocation, export/deletion, bounded signup/storage, CSP and encrypted backups followed. Foundation code 4d79e53 passed actual source CI . The original eight hosted browser journeys passed; a nonempty hosted snapshot was restored into an isolated local clone.
2. Add the editor without losing failure recovery Code cbd60fe added CodeMirror Markdown, safe preview/split, optional Vim, save shortcuts, exact Markdown downloads and dirty-navigation guards. The public example used the actual editor without an account or upload. Narrow split panes were stacked after phone review. Failed saves, expired sessions and a deliberately failed editor load were exercised; the plain editor fallback remained usable.
The collection passed 33 unit/React, 13 real PostgreSQL and 11 hosted browser checks. Editor record .
3. Connect notes by identity Code e1b8740 added stable ID links, explicit title ambiguity/missing states, linked-note pages, outgoing/backlink views and bounded graph navigation. A shared Markdown-aware scanner excluded code/HTML/existing links. Public example notes used no private API. Graph fitting and constant screen-size labels were corrected during visual review.
The collection passed 40 unit/React, 14 PostgreSQL and 14 hosted browser checks. Connected release and successful CI .
Successful check commands These are the repository’s actual release entrypoints. Database/browser commands need the isolated local PostgreSQL configuration described in the repository; never substitute an old production database URL.
npm ci npm run lint npm test npm run test:database npm run typecheck npm run build npm run test:browser Installed Next.js documentation was read before relevant API/component changes. Modal deployment uses the reviewed source allowlist, pinned Node image, existing noteweld-runtime secret and isolated Neon role. The owner used a private staged source directory to exclude credentials. The deploy entrypoint is:
python -m modal deploy app.py That command requires an authenticated Modal SDK environment and the established private runtime configuration. It does not create or approve accounts. Health is /api/health; encrypted snapshot/restore and incident steps are in operations .
Recorded failures and corrections Finding Correction and acceptance Early HTTP driver could not provide interactive transaction callbacks Use standard PostgreSQL driver; test actual rollback, duplicate races and ownership on disposable databases Original runtime dependencies had known advisories Compatible Next/sharp/source-map-js patches; rerun build, database/browser checks and runtime audit Narrow split editor and graph labels were difficult to read Stack panes and fit the visible graph while retaining readable screen-size labels; inspect phone screenshots Save conflict or failed network could lose confidence in a draft Preserve the draft and expose conflict/retry; exercise deliberate failures and recovery in the real browser Development-only upstream advisories remain documented. In-tab history is not a durable revision archive. Pageweft/Sonaweft bundle imports and commercial checkout were not implemented by these releases.
title: Building Noteweld: accounts to connected notes

description: From a Modal MinerU worker to source-aware exports, credit accounting and payment readiness.
text:
1. Establish actual extraction The initial requirement was private PDF-to-Markdown preparation using MinerU on the owner’s Modal account. The design moved from customer-provided Modal credentials to owner-hosted processing; customers do not provide cloud tokens. MinerU 2.7.6 runs in a cloud GPU image and retains original engine output. The laptop’s 2 GB GPU is not required.
A bounded one-page public trial was verified before describing full-book processing. The initial deployed web startup failed because modal_fn.py was missing from its uploaded source. Explicit inclusion fixed the image, followed by a fresh deployment and public workflow checks. Original verification record .
2. Make books and partial failure manageable Book inspection/ranges, explicit quotes, 20-page sections, partial outputs, selected retries, force OCR, cheaper CPU text extraction and cancellation were implemented. Source page indices were mapped back to the original PDF. Corrections/revision checks remained separate from engine output; exports preserved relative images, manifests, bookmarks and optional source PDF.
Actual GPU extraction checked selected pages from an original four-page fixture. A separate complete 1,000-page synthetic PDF passed the CPU text route across 50 sections with ordered pages and correct fixture-credit settlement. This proves that workflow on those sources; it does not prove scanned-book fidelity. Book release .
3. Account for usage and recovery The book ledger has one serialized writer, distinct from the older prototype ledger. Credit holds are reserved, settled or released transactionally; duplicate confirmation does not dispatch twice. Processing and file retention are separate from persistent financial records. Owner reports, admission envelopes, pause and encrypted snapshots were added. Admission estimates are not a whole-account cloud bill cap.
One-time $5/$10 packs replaced the earlier monthly access proposal. Rename commit 1372062 introduced Pageweft while retaining cloud/storage identities. Paddle integration commit e7a70ee superseded the Lemon Squeezy activation path. Signed events enter a durable inbox; fresh provider state and server-owned intents control grants/refunds. Current source has 78 automated checks; payment HTTP in those checks is mocked.
Successful commands and prerequisites The established owner deployment uses Python 3.13, authenticated Modal SDK 1.5.3, existing permanent session/payment secrets and separate ledger/results/model volumes. GPU dependencies run in the cloud image.
python3.13 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -q node --check static/app.js .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py For the recorded local browser fixture, with explicitly synthetic funds and real CPU text extraction:
.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn scripts.preview_books:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8768 Owner verification uses scripts.probe_deployed_books with an authorized original fixture and an explicit --mode text or --mode auto. Those probes seed internal verification credit; they are not purchases. scripts/test_e2e.py targets an older interface and is not the active release test.
Owner commands which were actually used for operations include:
.venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations report .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations backup Reports/backups remain private. Never publish a source book, recovery key, provider credential or decrypted ledger while reproducing them.
Recorded problems and current boundaries Finding Resolution or honest limit Missing deployed Python module prevented web startup Include the module explicitly and redeploy; check actual HTTPS rather than build output alone A whole-book job can partly fail Preserve successful sections and expose selected retry/cancellation; verify credit settlement and output order A budget estimate looked like a maximum invoice Separate admission envelopes, actual workspace billing, customer credit and cash contribution in operations Earlier monthly/BYO/Lemon assumptions no longer matched the product Owner-hosted processing, one-time packs and current Paddle integration supersede them without resetting balances Payment mocks passed but account approval was incomplete Keep checkout closed; complete identity/domain, real isolated provider tests and controlled live acceptance The dedicated payment checklist and Paddle release distinguish configured, tested and still-required steps. Representative difficult-document comparison and measured customer margin remain separate work.

description: The local CLI, actual cloud speech, optional review and the problems resolved before publication.
text:
Source chronology The original instascript command and import paths remain compatible. Hosted workbench 7fde01a added the upload/review/export workflow. 5ac1d7c added the original completed audio example; handoff 68b8472 normalized artifacts and corrected the provider reference. The old optional Claude/vault documents are archives, not required setup.
1. Preserve source and recover work The standalone CPU CLI uses FFmpeg/FFprobe and faster-whisper. Immutable original recognition, separate corrections, generated notes and sourced questions became distinct artifacts. Private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication support deliberate recovery; cross-path perceptual deduplication is not promised.
Versioned exports include Markdown/text/JSON/SRT/VTT and instascript-export/v1 provenance/hashes. A complete export is separate from implementing a future importer in Noteweld.
2. Run actual cloud recognition and bounded review The hosted FastAPI service uses separate Sonaweft ledger/media/model volumes. An on-demand Modal L4 loads the pinned large-v3 model revision in the cloud. The local MX350 does not host those weights. Optional DeepSeek text review has explicit consent, bounded text/output and schema/source-quote checks. Audio is not sent to that text API.
An original generated two-sentence recording was transcribed on local CPU, the Nix-built CLI and the cloud GPU. Actual configured DeepSeek Flash review succeeded; the advanced model was listed by the API, not inference-benchmarked. The combined cloud pipeline and public upload/correction/export journey passed.
3. Add accounting and public evidence The single ledger writer reserves a quoted amount once and settles only a completed selected package. Failures release reservations; explicit retry may reuse retained recognition. Paddle product/prices and a paused notification were configured separately from Pageweft. Fresh transaction/adjustment reads enforce server-owned intent, owner, product and environment. No shared wallet is implemented.
Fifty-two automated checks, source CI and real hosted browser acceptance are recorded in the release . Those payment API tests are mocked. An actual encrypted remote financial snapshot was decrypted into a disposable SQLite clone and passed integrity/balance checks; it does not restore expired media.
Successful commands Start with Python 3.13 and separately available FFmpeg/FFprobe. Install only the extras needed for the selected local/cloud workflow.
python3.13 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install '.[web,cloud]' bin/sonaweft recording.mp3 --out ./out python -m unittest discover -s tests -q node --check sonaweft_web/static/app.js node --check sonaweft_web/static/checkout.js .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py recording.mp3 is a placeholder for an authorized local recording, not a distributed third-party fixture. The deployment requires owner authentication and the already-established session/payment/LLM secrets. Provider values stay server-side. The tested Nix route was:
nix build .#default --no-link The resulting CLI actually processed the generated recording; no NixOS rebuild was needed. Owner reports and encrypted snapshots use scripts/operations.py; the exact incident/payment sequence is in operations .
Recorded failures and fixes Observed problem Implemented correction Cloud exception/NumPy values could not cross the function boundary Return native JSON values and a plain error envelope; rerun actual combined cloud processing PyAV 19 broke the tested pip speech dependency combination Pin pip/cloud to tested PyAV 15.1.0; keep Nix’s separately validated compatible pair distinct Nix dynamic-library discovery hit SIGPIPE in the launcher Correct the discovery path and run the Nix-built CLI on the original audio A completed audio sample needed actual evidence rather than an illustrative VTT Publish the original generated recording, real recognition/review and a manifest-verified bundle; verify playback/seek/download No long/noisy/audio-accent benchmark, diarization, hosted arbitrary-URL import, immediate self-service deletion or live merchant approval is implied. Checkout remains closed until actual account and payment acceptance.

description: What the native-browser implementation contains, what was reviewed locally and what remains unpublished.
text:
Keep the two implementations separate This is the vanilla JavaScript/localStorage application, not Noteweld. Native DOM modules, Webpack, checklists, labels, colors, pin/archive/trash and browser storage form its implementation. Existing source history includes f6bc24ce for labels/search/filter/demo notes and 64471b8d for an unused import cleanup.
The 16 October reliability release incorporates the preserved local changes and intentional tracked-dependency cleanup. Source commit a03b0ed1 publishes the browser reliability work; the portfolio refresh copies its production bundle. Earlier statements below describe the baseline they reviewed.
Local reliability work The current source notes describe versioned JSON backups, validation-before-write, ID-preserving merge and attempted rollback after failed import writes. Tests use jsdom for storage/backup/checklist boundaries. They are not evidence of every visible browser journey. That earlier review identified unfinished header search, placeholder reminders, storage-error recovery and mobile/accessibility defects. The release below addresses those confirmed defects.
Build and copy the demo The documented development entrypoints use Node 24:
npm ci npm test npm run build The generated dist/ is separate from editable src/. The portfolio keeps its own copied bundle under demos/keep/. The established copy operation is:
rsync -a --delete ../Keep/dist/ demos/keep/ Run that last command from the portfolio only after reviewing the source build. It replaces only the copied demo directory. It is not a command to run against a source or home directory. Its presence in the manual does not assert that unpublished local changes have been copied into the currently served demo.
Actual portfolio acceptance The portfolio browser checks exercised opening/closing the copied demo, iframe unloading and focus restoration at phone/desktop sizes. Later portfolio DOM checks preserved those paths while adding Pageweft previews and the Hugo library. This establishes the embedding/interaction boundary, not every internal storage/import path of a new vanilla release.
Failures and limits retained instead of hidden A browser-local store is not cloud persistence; different origins/profiles/devices do not share notes. A README/source update can be ahead of the copied distribution; keep build/copy/release evidence separate. Import rollback is not proof that every storage-quota failure elsewhere has a good recovery flow. Earlier license wording was inconsistent with the package declaration; no new license was silently selected. There is no claim that the vanilla demo already contains Noteweld’s Markdown/Vim/graph or account features. Broader non-paid feature parity remains a separate future collection.
Reliability release — 16 October 2026 The release connects both search controls, refreshes imported labels immediately and gives icon controls accessible names. Native edit dialogs contain focus and return it on Escape. Colored notes use readable text, narrow layouts fit 320/390/768/1440-pixel viewports, and keyboard users can navigate the sidebar and composer.
Quota failures retain open drafts and expose retry. Invalid saved JSON is preserved for raw recovery instead of being overwritten with samples. A regression test caught Archive deleting directly; it now moves to Trash, with confirmation before permanent deletion. Another caught the expanded sidebar covering Archive controls after navigation; main-content spacing now follows the actual sidebar state.
The original development dependencies produced audit findings. Compatible updates reduced them, but a remaining unpatched braces dependency came from webpack-dev-server. A small Node loopback preview now serves only explicitly allowed generated assets while Webpack watches source files. It provides manual refresh instead of hot reload. The final audit reported zero vulnerabilities; no forced downgrade or advisory suppression was used.
Checks: 14 unit tests, 22 Chromium journeys and a production build passed. Automated WCAG A/AA checks passed for seeded phone/desktop screens. Tracked node_modules and generated dist files were removed from source tracking; the existing intentional dependency removals were included, and CI builds from the lockfile with Node 24. Existing local browser-data keys and public URLs remain compatible.
The record does not claim an automatic backup service, cloud synchronization, a reminder scheduler or full professional-product parity.

description: A short reading route from visible features to source, tests and operational boundaries.
text:
Start with behavior Open a project’s usage guide and its live or completed example. Identify the intended action, what should persist, the expected failure behavior and the current limits. A polished cover illustration is not a running backend.
Follow the implementation Read the technical overview, then the specific architecture/editor/connections manual. Imported documents link an exact committed source revision. A local documentation edition is marked when it includes uncommitted documentation changes; the link then identifies the committed baseline.
Interpret evidence precisely Static checks establish particular code/build properties. Unit tests can substitute model, network or authentication boundaries. Database tests establish behavior on an actual disposable database. Browser journeys exercise visible flows and selected failure cases. Hosted checks establish observed behavior at a real deployment at that time. A real model call is separate from a difficult-document/audio benchmark. Mock payment tests do not establish seller approval, real delivery or payout. Read release dates and the current project status together. An older release can truthfully say that a feature was still future work even when a later release has shipped it.
Prepare for the code audit Choose one project and feature collection at a time. Trace a representative request from interface through validation, processing/storage and error recovery. Review the corresponding tests and reproduce the meaningful checks before changing behavior. Never put real customer documents, recovery keys or credentials into screenshots or public issues.
A personalized learning list and Upwork proposal/interview workflow are follow-up work; the existence of this manual is not evidence that either has already been completed.
title: How to review these projects

description: The actual configured editing workflow: Telescope, Harpoon, language servers, formatting and Markdown.
text:
Follow a small loop Find a file, make a focused change, inspect diagnostics, format it, and run the relevant check. The editor shortens that loop; it does not establish that a change is correct.
The configured leader is Space. These mappings come from the published Neovim source , inspected alongside the local checkout.
Action Configured mapping Tool Find project files Space, s, f Telescope Search file contents Space, s, g Telescope live grep Remember a working file Space, a Harpoon Open the remembered-file menu Ctrl + e Harpoon Format a buffer Space, f Conform Move between editor splits Ctrl + h / j / k / l Neovim window navigation Language support through Nix The Neovim wrapper supplies language-server and formatter executables: gopls, TypeScript language server, nil, Pyright, clangd, Lua language server, Marksman and rust-analyzer among them. Formatting tools include Stylua, nixfmt, gofumpt, Black and Ruff.
This avoids depending on ordinary Linux binary downloads that may assume filesystem paths unavailable on NixOS. Plugin configuration and language-server behavior still need testing for the particular project.
Code and technical writing The setup includes Treesitter grammars, Telescope, Harpoon, Conform and Markdown-oriented tooling. It supports moving between source code and technical notes while keeping tools close to the current buffer.
The Workbench’s browser editor demonstrates a deliberately small subset: h/j/k/l movement, i for insert, Escape for normal mode, x for deletion and u for undo. File switching retains each temporary buffer within the page. It is an interactive keyboard sketch of the workflow, with native browser controls available throughout.
Verification boundary An actual headless Neovim startup succeeded on 16 October, and twelve selected language-server/formatter executables resolved inside its wrapped environment. That check does not certify every plugin, language server or debugger. The next deeper check is a representative edit/diagnostic/format/test journey for each language actually used on a client project.
title: Neovim: find, edit, inspect

description: A practical maintenance sequence that keeps source review, builds, activation and real runtime evidence distinct.
text:
Review before changing the system Inspect Git state and the relevant diff. Back up files being changed privately. Preserve unrelated work, the current lock file and a known working boot generation. New files referenced by a Git-backed flake must be deliberately included in its source.
Use a Git-filtered flake source. An explicit unfiltered path: source may include ignored private files before a build-time check can reject them.
Match the check to the change Change Relevant evidence Documentation Generated pages, links, keyboard and browser checks User-profile application Package build, executable, launch and a real file operation NixOS service Option evaluation, system build, activation and actual service behavior Graphics/kernel update Supported hardware branch, complete build, rollback route and controlled boot acceptance Backup procedure Retained-data fixtures, successful real copy and a separate restore test For this machine, the nr shortcut runs sudo nixos-rebuild switch against the NixOS flake. It does not decrypt secrets, stage files or commit changes. Administrative authentication remains an operating-system boundary.
The verified maintenance example The 16 October security pass enabled the stateful firewall, restricted local DNS, separated root’s editor from mutable personal Lua, removed the global browser decoder-sandbox override, and removed unattended Git publication. The non-deleting HDD copy was repaired and actually completed. Syncthing received HDD mount guards and private-file exclusions; Unicode filename conflicts were corrected while preserving both original byte copies.
The system build also runs a source-hygiene check and eight backup-copy tests with disposable data. A successful build, an activated configuration and a working service are recorded separately.
Recovery remains explicit The same-machine HDD copies and legacy Borg repository are not an independent encrypted recovery plan. Credential recovery, backup encryption and a controlled system/driver upgrade remain separate work. Existing browser processes inherit their startup environment until restarted. An offline paired phone prevents an end-to-end sync observation even when local checks pass.
The original public configuration predates this local maintenance pass. Publishing a reviewed source revision is a separate step; the guides do not represent the baseline repository as already containing unpublished changes.
For software delivery, the same discipline applies: local tests, real persistence, browser journeys, CI, deployed checks and recovery each answer a different question. See how to read the evidence .

description: Where the Markdown lives, how reviewed snapshots are refreshed and how Hugo reaches GitHub Pages.
text:
Source and publication The actual portfolio repository contains documentation/ for Hugo source and manuals/ for generated static output. The existing GitHub Pages root serves both the portfolio and /manuals/. No application server, visitor login, external font, analytics service or search API is needed.
Hugo 0.156.0 is the recorded build version. Imported project README/docs files are explicitly listed in documentation/manifest.json; this is not a recursive copy of the workspace. Current usage guides and journal entries are authored directly in Hugo content.
Refresh a reviewed source snapshot From the portfolio repository, inspect the documentation changes in the sibling project first. New files require an explicit manifest review. Then run:
python3 scripts/sync-manuals.py python3 scripts/sync-manuals.py --check python3 scripts/build-docs.py python3 scripts/build-docs.py --check python3 scripts/check-docs.py node tests/portfolio.test.mjs Source revisions and content hashes are recorded in the source inventory . Imported links point to the corresponding manual or exact GitHub source revision. Downloads contain the reviewed public edition and provenance. Synchronization is explicit; this is not a live mirror of private workspace changes.
Review and publish Preview the repository with a local static HTTP server. Check mobile layout, search, keyboard navigation, Markdown downloads and relevant portfolio controls. Review the diff for secrets, personal notes, source books and misleading claims before committing. Push the reviewed portfolio main branch to use its existing Pages publication; check the completed deployment and actual public pages.
The build script uses a temporary directory, verifies the pinned Hugo version and replaces only generated manuals/ output. Its check mode compares every generated file. Source Markdown and existing portfolio/demo assets are not deleted by that build. Restoring a previous portfolio commit rolls back the static publication without changing application databases.
Included and excluded material All reviewed README/docs records from the four active portfolio implementations are represented by the explicit manifest. Current guides, technical references, operations and release records are rendered. Five obsolete/personal-planning documents get clearly labeled archive entries that link their existing source instead of copying obsolete commands or personal conversation. Owner-specific questions at the end of the Pageweft launch register are omitted.
Agent instructions, private environment files, customer uploads, untracked work, generated transcripts, extracted books, original source PDFs and startup/business paperwork are outside this library. Existing unrelated working changes remain in their own repositories. Private evidence files are not uploaded to the site.
Future entries Add ordinary Markdown under documentation/content/journal/ with a title, date and description, then rebuild. The home page lists new entries and publishes an RSS feed. Search reads a static generated JSON index in the visitor’s browser; no query is sent to a search provider. Without JavaScript, project navigation and manuals remain readable.

description: What the current providers do, reproducible cost examples and the remaining payment sequence.
text:
Neon in this application Neon hosts PostgreSQL. Noteweld connects through standard pg/Drizzle and stores accounts, notes, labels, revisions and recovery/session state there. Modal runs the Node application; the two providers have separate roles. Moving the database later needs migration/connection configuration, not a replacement for SQL.
Neon supports autoscaling, idle suspension and branching. Its advertised Free tier currently includes 100 CU-hours and 1 GB per project. That is a published allowance, not verification of an individual account plan. Neon overview , pricing , checked 16 October 2026.
Modal rates and the actual configured work Modal pricing , checked 16 October 2026: Starter has no fixed monthly plan fee and includes $30/month compute per workspace. Base per-second rates are A10 $0.000306, L4 $0.000222, CPU $0.0000131/core and memory $0.00000222/GiB. Volumes include 1 TiB/month, then $0.09/GiB-month; Starter egress includes 1 TiB/month, then $0.04/GiB. These apps use Functions, not the differently priced Sandboxes or token-priced Shared Endpoints.
Compute is billed for load, processing and the configured warm tail. CPU/memory use is charged at least at the request. Pageweft’s GPU sections request/cap two cores and 8 GiB; Noteweld requests 0.25 core/1.5 GiB, with higher CPU usage possible. Sonaweft’s speech function does not declare the same fixed CPU/RAM envelope, so its GPU rate alone is not its total invoice.
Explicit container-region selection adds a multiplier: 1.15 for broad regions and 1.75 for a narrow region such as Noteweld’s region="us-east". A .us-east.modal.run routing hostname alone does not establish that container-region surcharge. Region selection , resource requests .
Reproducible illustrations, before credits These are calculations from assumed billed resource-seconds, not measured conversion speed or a forecast of per-user consumption.
Work assumption Gross estimate A10 + 2 CPU cores + 8 GiB for one billed hour $1.2599 100 GPU worker runs, each using that envelope for 120 billed seconds $4.20 1,000 such worker runs $42.00 L4 alone for one billed hour; CPU/RAM still additional $0.7992 Noteweld at requested CPU/RAM for 10 active hours, including its 1.75 region factor $0.42 A document can require several worker runs; these rows do not assume one document equals one GPU run. All applications and private owner workloads share the workspace’s allowance; there is not another $30 for each app. At $42 gross eligible compute, roughly $12 would remain after an otherwise-unused $30 allowance. Add other applications, startup/warm time, actual resource use, noncovered items and tax as applicable. Credits improve the immediate bill but should not define long-term customer margin.
Count jobs, selected pages, measured billed GPU seconds, active web time, retained data and external LLM tokens. Registered-user count alone does not determine hosting cost. A 1,000-page text-only synthetic extraction is not evidence of GPU time for a difficult scanned book.
Control spending deliberately Owner reports can read the actual workspace’s metered and billed totals; those private financial snapshots are not published here. Internal Pageweft/Sonaweft admission envelopes are separate from provider limits. Modal budgets distinguishes a gross usage budget and a monthly net out-of-pocket spend limit. A saved global limit has not been verified by these releases. Selecting one affects every workload sharing the account, so it must be an explicit owner choice. There is no reason to upgrade to Team merely to keep these small previews online.
Paddle: configured versus still required Pageweft and Sonaweft have separate configured products, $5/$10 prices, runtime/client configuration and paused notification destinations. The last observed website status on 15 October was In review. This page does not represent a fresh seller-dashboard approval check. Both checkouts remain closed. Noteweld has no paid checkout; the retained Go study and vanilla demo do not need one.
The remaining operational sequence is:
Complete Paddle’s requested seller/identity verification with correct legal details. Its process includes domain review and identity verification; business verification differs for individuals/sole traders. Account verification . Obtain approval for each actual product hostname and the processing-pack business model; finalize operator/contact/pricing/privacy/refund pages against the real seller identity. Test in a separate Paddle sandbox with isolated products, webhook secret and ledger. Cover purchase, abandonment, genuine signed duplicate/reordered delivery, refunds, chargebacks, provider outage and recovery. Current mocked tests do not replace this. Finish the approved default payment link, payment methods, tax presentation, balance currency and correct payout details. Validate server-side keys/signatures; enable only the intended notification destination. Go-live checklist . After approval and sandbox acceptance, conduct an explicit controlled live purchase/refund and reconcile the real provider receipt/ledger. Open normal paid access only when those checks pass. Payout acceptance is an additional check, not something a browser success page proves. Maintain credentials. Existing recorded runtime-key expiry is 13 January 2027, with rotation targeted before 6 January; update both products if the runtime key is still shared. Never publish keys or recovery secrets. Paddle’s published default fee is 5% + $0.50 per checkout: a simplified $5 purchase leaves $4.25 and $10 leaves $9 before other effects. Under-$10 custom pricing is by agreement, not automatic. Payout documentation describes monthly payouts, a minimum $100 threshold and possible wire/bank charges. A small sale therefore does not mean immediate cash in a bank account.
Use the detailed project-specific Pageweft activation and Sonaweft operations records when executing the steps. This is not an account-approval claim or an instruction to activate checkout now.

description: LocalStorage behavior, setup, backup/import design and known release work.
text:
A free, browser-only notes and checklist demo built with native DOM APIs, CSS, localStorage and Webpack. It shares Noteweld’s product family and deliberately has no account, server or paid features. The existing Keep repository and public URL are preserved.
Live demo · Source · Portfolio and manuals Features Create and edit notes and checklists; pin, color, label, archive, trash and restore them. Search titles, bodies, labels and checklist text from either search control. Use keyboard navigation, named controls and a focus-contained edit dialog; Escape saves and returns focus. Export versioned JSON including archived/trashed notes and labels; validate and merge imports without replacing existing IDs. Preserve drafts when a storage write fails, display an error and allow retry. Recover raw stored JSON if existing notes are malformed, without silently resetting user data. Use a responsive layout with readable colored notes and reduced-motion support. Delete from Archive moves to recoverable Trash. Delete forever and Empty Trash require confirmation. There is no automatic seven-day purge. Header Refresh reloads this browser view; the layout control switches compact display. Placeholder reminders/settings are omitted from the available controls.
Run and verify Use Node.js 24. Development serves only on loopback.
npm ci npm run dev # Open http://localhost:3000 npm test npm run build npx playwright install chromium npm run test:e2e npm audit On NixOS, use an installed compatible Chromium via PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/run/current-system/sw/bin/chromium. The lockfile pins tested dependencies. A small loopback-only Node server serves the generated demo; Webpack watches source changes, and you refresh the page to see them. It has no proxy, uploads or hot-reload service. Unit tests cover storage, backup validation/rollback and checklist editing. Browser tests exercise persistence, import/export, keyboard controls, failed saves, corrupt-data recovery and four viewport widths. Automated accessibility checks supplement keyboard and visual review; they do not certify every possible user journey.
The Pages workflow builds dist/ from source. The portfolio embeds a copy of that production bundle; a release must update both and verify public pages.
Code map src/index.js: boot, recovery and shared DOM helpers. src/header/, src/side/: search and keyboard navigation. src/main/notes/notes-store.js: persisted notes and labels. src/main/notes/backup.js: validated, additive JSON portability. src/main/notes/checklist-editor.js: checklist UI. src/main/notes/notes.js: composer, edit dialog, cards and filters. src/main/notes/storage-feedback.js: visible persistence failures. src/main/archive/, src/main/trash/: recovery and explicit deletion. tests/: unit and browser acceptance cases. Boundaries This is a local demo, with no cloud sync, login, payments, reminder scheduler, Markdown/Vim editor or graph. Export important notes before clearing browser data. Different sites/origins have separate storage, while the portfolio and its embedded demo share an origin; avoid putting sensitive material in a showcase.
The package declares ISC; no standalone license file was present in the original repository. This release does not invent an MIT grant or change asset ownership. The active Noteweld mark is original SVG code, fonts come from the operating system, and the inactive legacy Keep image is no longer bundled. Full non-paid feature parity with the professional product remains a later scope.

description: Architecture, implemented scope, setup and the current release.
text:
Public address and existing-account access Account enhancement work on feat/account-signin is local and gated; setup, behavior and remaining acceptance . Existing public hosting is unchanged. Google/GitHub login is not publicly verified by these source changes. A private notes/checklist preview built with Next.js 16.3.8, React 19, Auth.js and PostgreSQL/Drizzle. This repository retains its original keep-nextjs GitHub identity. The old Vercel deployment is a historical version; it is not updated by this release.
Implemented Real account/seed transactions; normalized unique email and label identities; exact passphrases, with 15-character minimum and bcrypt’s 72-byte UTF-8 limit. Cookie authentication, hashed one-time recovery keys, key rotation, session revocation on recovery and account deletion. No email verification/reset provider is connected. Notes, checklists, pin/colour/archive/trash, labels and search; shared navigation updates and narrow-screen drawer. Stable wiki links, an owned connection index, outgoing/backlink lists and authenticated linked-note pages, including archive and explicit missing/ambiguous targets. A bounded note graph with label/title filters, neighbourhood focus, fit/zoom/pan and equivalent keyboard/list navigation. Explore the account-free graph . Markdown source editing with CodeMirror, optional Vim keys, undo/redo, in-note find/replace, formatting, safe GFM preview and split view. A simple textarea remains available. Try the account-free editor . Exact .md downloads, explicit save shortcuts and retained undo when switching standard/Vim keys or write/preview/split views. Saved-version reload starts fresh history; server revisions protect against concurrent changes rather than storing a permanent revision archive. Explicit saves, preserved failed drafts, bounded requests, idempotent creation and revision conflicts instead of silent overwrites. Trash permits restoration or confirmed permanent deletion. Snapshot-based empty trash, account JSON export, confirmed passphrase-protected account deletion, no-cache private responses and nonce-based production script CSP. Bounded free preview: 100 accounts, 50 registrations/day, 250 notes, 50 labels and 2 MiB note text/account. PostgreSQL-backed admission limits and one scale-to-zero CPU web container. Not implemented: Sonaweft/Pageweft bundle imports, bare hashtag parsing, global Vim navigation, durable revision history, paid access, reminders, offline sync, collaboration and end-to-end encryption. Those follow this connected-notes milestone. This is not a production SLA or a place for irreplaceable/sensitive material.
Read the connected-notes guide and current release evidence . Graph bounds and title-vs-ID semantics are explicit; original note source remains the stored/exported format with no schema migration.
The /example scratchpad needs no account and never uploads its content. In that demo Ctrl/Cmd-S and :w download Markdown; in the private workspace they save to the account. Drafts and undo live in the current tab. Read the editor guide and current editor release evidence ; foundation evidence is the 15 October baseline.
Isolated local development Node 24 and PostgreSQL 17 are required. flake.lock pins the Nix development inputs; it does not change NixOS or graphics drivers.
nix develop npm ci node scripts/local-db.mjs start node scripts/isolated.mjs migrate node scripts/isolated.mjs dev # http://localhost:3107 The helper creates a private loopback-only PostgreSQL cluster in ignored .local/, using SCRAM for TCP and a private owner-only socket. It refuses unmarked existing database directories. Tests never fall back to the application’s .env.local or existing hosted database. Use node scripts/local-db.mjs stop when finished. CI instead supplies a disposable loopback NOTEWELD_TEST_DATABASE_URL.
For a separate ordinary installation, copy .env.example into .env.local, fill in your own new development database, migrate with npx drizzle-kit migrate, then npm run dev. Never point tests at production. Missing DATABASE_URL is an error, not a dummy fallback. Hosted Neon uses the standard pg driver and verified TLS, not the old HTTP batch adapter.
Verification npm test # Unit and React/jsdom boundary checks npm run lint npm run typecheck npm run test:database # Real transactions, quotas, ownership, recovery, migration rollback and restore node scripts/isolated.mjs build # Production build, disposable DB config npm run test:browser # Real cookie/PostgreSQL journey + explicit failure simulations Browser binaries are separate: inside nix develop the shell selects Chromium. Else install the pinned Playwright browser with npx playwright install --with-deps chromium on a supported distribution, or set PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH to a tested system Chromium. Chromium’s sandbox stays enabled. NOTEWELD_BROWSER_URL explicitly targets an existing preview; absent that variable, Playwright starts its own isolated port 3107 server and refuses to reuse an unrelated server. Synthetic accounts are deleted after the full journey. Failed tests may leave synthetic accounts in the disposable database.
Tests do not capture authentication screenshots, traces or video. Optional NOTEWELD_SCREENSHOTS=.local/browser captures only the authenticated note workspace at four widths. Mocked failures are labelled separately from actual database and full-session checks. See release evidence .
Hosting and operations app.py builds from an explicit source allowlist on a digest-pinned official Node image, using npm ci. It never uploads .env, .local or the whole workspace. Only Next’s standalone runtime, static assets and owner tooling run in the cloud. requirements-operations.txt pins the Modal/crypto SDKs. See operations for isolated roles, deployment, backup/restore and rollback.
src/app/api/ owns runtime validation/auth boundaries. src/components/WorkspaceContext.tsx owns label/draft coordination; useNotes ignores stale requests. src/db/migrations/ holds forward migrations, including legacy-collision protection. Existing source/working changes were preserved before this foundation was implemented; there is no automatic merge/delete of conflicting legacy accounts.
The point-in-time runtime audit is clean after the 16.3.8 security patches. Development-only glob/esbuild advisories and their exact boundaries are recorded in release evidence ; the full dependency graph is not claimed vulnerability-free.

description: Features, extraction architecture, local setup, cloud deployment and limits.
text:

Hosted PDF-to-Markdown conversion for books and technical material, using MinerU on Amir’s Modal account. Inspect selected pages, review issues, correct text and export portable files for your own editor or LLM workflow.
Live bounded sample · Custom domain / existing workspace recovery · Launch register / remaining steps · Owner operations · Implemented features / pricing / evidence · Payment activation Current implementation Books up to 64 MiB / 1,000 PDF pages; inspect up to five PDFs, each confirmed separately. Original PDF page selection, price confirmation and text-layer inspection before extraction. Automatic or forced OCR with pinned MinerU 2.7.6; cheaper explicit text-only extraction without GPU/OCR/images. Bounded 20-page sections, persistent jobs, partial output, cancellation and selective reprocessing. Source-page review, symptom reports, corrections with history and stale-edit protection. Single-file, per-page, page-group or PDF-bookmark exports with relative image paths, original engine output, manifests and optional source PDF. Private session ownership, account recovery key, source/output deletion and 48-hour file expiry. Transactional processing-credit reserve/settle/release and one-time pack integration. Paddle catalog, runtime credentials and signed-payment integration are configured; merchant review and real payment delivery remain pending. Private owner dashboard, actual Modal workspace billing readout, conservative admission budgets/pause, aggregated activity/error counts and encrypted financial snapshots. Actual provider-level spend limits and commercial margins remain separate verification. Original public PDF/Markdown/ZIP example and practical conversion guide, canonical pages and crawl metadata; no search ranking or user acquisition claim. No recurring access fee. Launch tariff: MinerU $0.50/job + $0.005/selected page; text-only $0.25 + $0.001/page. One-time packs are configured at $5/$10; checkout remains closed pending approval and payment verification. Reprocessing completed pages has a $0.20 service fee plus page usage; failed-page retry does not repeat an already charged initial fee. Credits do not expire; files/edits do. This is a service tariff, not exact measured compute pass-through or guaranteed net profit.
Architecture Browser: encrypted session + CSRF | inspect PDF / review quote / confirm v Modal CPU FastAPI (web/studio.py) | | v v Serialized book_store Private source/section volume | books.sqlite ^ | atomic credit holds | v | CPU coordinator -> bounded GPU or CPU text workers | successful section settles once; failure releases allowance v Source-aware pages -> corrections/history -> portable ZIP export Signed payment event + fresh provider order -> grant/revoke credits once Hourly cleanup -> expired files; credit/account records remain separate The active ledger is /ledger/books.sqlite; the original prototype’s /ledger/state.sqlite is preserved separately. Each has one writer function. Do not run a second app/writer on the same volume. Owner probes invoke deployed functions. The original authenticated extract_pdf remains available for preparation scripts; no public Modal credentials are collected.
Initial CPU/GPU concurrency, page-attempt and upload caps are listed in release notes . This is a bounded early service, not demonstrated thousands-of-concurrent-user capacity. OCR can damage symbols or lose content; review flags and source metadata do not certify correctness. Unknown blocks and original engine output remain available for inspection.
Development and deployment Python 3.13; Modal SDK 1.5.3. GPU image uses Python 3.12. Direct package versions are pinned; transitive/model revisions are not all pinned. No local AI weights or GPU setup are required.
python3.13 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -q node --check static/app.js .venv/bin/ruff check --select E9,F63,F7,F82,F401 web/books.py web/credits.py web/documents.py web/studio.py .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py Owner Modal authentication is required. Keep the existing Fernet key in document-studio-session; changing it invalidates sessions and key-derived recovery identities. The separate document-studio-payments secret contains scoped Paddle runtime configuration with BILLING_MODE=test and PADDLE_SELLER_APPROVED=false; merchant review is pending. Public test-mode grants are disabled. See activation steps before live charging.
For a local browser fixture with real text extraction and explicit synthetic credit, run:
.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn scripts.preview_books:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8768 This fixture is not deployed, does not process payments or run local MinerU, and supports text-only execution. For owner-only cloud verification through existing deployed functions, use .venv/bin/python -m scripts.probe_deployed_books --pdf <original-test.pdf> --mode text or --mode auto. It seeds an explicit internal credit fixture; this does not verify a purchase. Historical scripts/test_e2e.py targets the retired SSE/BYO interface and is not the active release test.
Verification and limits The current 78-test automated suite, real Modal extraction, live public trial/edit/export and responsive browser evidence are recorded in BOOK-RELEASE.md . A complete 1,000-page synthetic PDF passed deployed text-layer extraction across 50 sections with all pages exported and correct credit settlement; this is not a GPU whole-book fidelity benchmark. Paddle validation/signature/refund tests use synthetic HTTP and real disposable SQLite. Dedicated checkout, recovery and public policy pages passed local and deployed Chromium checks at 320/390/768/1440 pixels; no real Paddle payment or sandbox purchase was performed. See Paddle evidence . Representative difficult-document comparison and real merchant delivery remain distinct work.
Results are private through session ownership, not a claim of zero provider retention. Hard-killed workers reconcile through deadlines; uncertain dispatch never automatically spends on a retry. Scheduled cleanup, storage, cache and compute can incur charges. Shared-IP trial limits can affect legitimate users.
Unmodified MinerU 2.7.6 source / AGPL-3.0 release attribution is visible in the UI. Dependency notes distinguish exact-release licensing from current upstream master. New books, extracted collections, credentials, local environments and test artifacts are ignored. Historical tracked sources already exist; this change does not remove them or rewrite history.

description: Hosted workflow, processing tariff, local CLI, deployment and limits.
text:
Open Sonaweft · Hear completed example · Product contract · Operations · Release evidence Turn authorized recordings into timestamped transcripts, editable drafts, subtitles and portable Markdown. Hear each segment while correcting it. Original speech recognition, your corrections and optional AI notes remain separate. Formerly instaScript / Transcript Studio; existing commands, Python imports and GitHub URLs remain compatible.
Hosted workflow Upload English audio/video, up to 64 MiB / 60 minutes; inspection returns a quote without starting transcription. Confirm media rights, then request a bounded 30-second sample or paid processing when commercial access opens. Optionally consent to sending transcript text to DeepSeek for standard/deeper review. Audio is not sent to DeepSeek. Follow the job, hear timestamped segments, search text and save separate corrections with revision checks. Export original Markdown/text/JSON/SRT/VTT, corrected Markdown/JSON, optional summary/research questions and a hashed instascript-export/v1 manifest. AI suggestions never silently replace the original. Source questions quote actual segments; explicit Crossref lookup returns scholarly metadata candidates, not factual verdicts. Hosted URL downloads, diarization, speaker identification and certified transcription are not implemented; use an authorized upload or the local CLI.
The sample is once per workspace/IP hash, subject to three global samples/day, twenty/month and additional admission/storage caps. Sources/results expire after 48 hours with hourly cleanup. Paid packs remain closed pending Paddle seller/website approval and real payment acceptance tests. No card is needed for an available sample.
Service pricing One-time $5 / $10 processing packs, no recurring access fee. Credit is reserved before dispatch and consumed only when the complete selected result succeeds; failure returns the full reservation. Explicit retries get a fresh quote and can reuse retained ASR.
Processing Per job Per started minute 60 minutes Transcription $0.15 $0.015 $1.05 With standard review $0.25 $0.020 $1.45 With advanced review $0.35 $0.025 $1.85 Applicable tax is handled at checkout. These are service tariffs, not exact provider reimbursements or guaranteed margins. Sonaweft/Pageweft balances are independent processing entitlements.
Local CLI Python 3.13 is the tested pip environment. Install FFmpeg/FFprobe and yt-dlp separately. Local recognition uses CPU/int8; downloaded models and optional provider charges are the operator’s responsibility.
python3.13 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install . bin/sonaweft recording.mp3 --out ./out bin/sonaweft 'https://example.org/authorized-media' --out ./out bin/sonaweft --queue ./queue.md --out ./out bin/sonaweft recording.mp3 --review --review-model standard --out ./out bin/sonaweft --export-item ./out/ITEM --format vtt The launchers resolve NixOS wheel libraries dynamically, prefer an existing tested .venv-web, otherwise .venv; SONAWEFT_PYTHON overrides. title: Technical overview

description: Design rationale and evaluation criteria; the usage guide describes current availability.
text:
Implementation update The approved core features are now implemented: full-book/range inspection (bounded at 64 MiB/1,000 pages), batch inspection, quotes, bounded section processing, selective retries/force OCR, source-linked review, corrections/history, portable outputs and prepaid-credit accounting. Read BOOK-RELEASE.md for tested evidence and limits. Earlier candidate language below describes the design rationale. Actual merchant activation and comparative difficult-document fidelity remain unverified; these features do not certify every source symbol.
Pageweft: conversion utility User clarification, 14 October 2026: PDF-to-Markdown for serious work with books, including Linguavell preparation. Users control the downstream reading/LLM workflow. No study platform, AI chat, automatically generated teaching materials or decorative feature expansion.
Product hypothesis Turn difficult books and technical PDFs into portable, source-traceable Markdown with less manual repair and predictable processing costs. Modal is infrastructure; MinerU is a selected engine. Customers buy the result and saved setup/repair time, not the provider combination.
Strongest initial cohort: repeated book/PDF conversion users who want plain files for their own editor, scripts or LLM. Students/scientists are qualified by this concrete need, not by profession or document volume alone. An occasional converter may reasonably reject a monthly subscription; validate actual return usage rather than assuming continuing demand.
Existing verified foundation Owner-hosted pinned MinerU 2.7.6 with private CLI worker; no customer Modal credentials. One-selected-page bounded public trial after book inspection; per-session/IP quotas and global admission controls. These are not a provider-wide invoice limit. Persistent serialized job/quota ledger, duplicate-request suppression and session-owned downloads. Markdown/images, original PDF, available source block/page metadata and navigation, detectable replacement glyph and missing-image report. Real public synthetic PDF upload → conversion → ZIP download passed. This does not establish book fidelity, rendered Markdown compatibility across editors, medical accuracy or complete coverage for every PDF page. Current pricing uses one-time $5/$10 processing packs without recurring access fees; transactional credit accounting is implemented. Actual seller activation and payment delivery remain unverified. The former monthly access model is superseded. Original design rationale (core now implemented; evidence in BOOK-RELEASE.md) Book handling: accept suitably bounded full books; allow selected PDF pages/ranges; split work into bounded sections; join output without losing images or order; preserve original PDF page references. Retries must rerun only failed selected work. The current public trial and disabled 50-page paid draft do not satisfy this requirement. Fidelity: evaluate reading order, headings, paragraphs, hyphenation, footnotes, tables, formulas and specialized Unicode/IPA against rendered source pages. Flag detectable defects separately from unchecked correctness; do not silently guess or paraphrase the source. Portable files: standard Markdown plus documented extensions when needed, relative local image paths, one-document or section exports, optional PDF-page links. Reprocessing must not change unaffected filenames or introduce duplicate pages. Keep raw engine output separate from optional normalization. Review and repair: show reported defects and the relevant source page; preserve the user’s edits. Allow selected-page re-extraction with visible price and changes. No promise of automatic perfect error detection or universally accurate OCR. Predictable cost: show a bounded quote before confirmation; reserve processing funds transactionally; settle measured/defined tariff costs; release unused funds; handle failed jobs according to disclosed rules; prevent duplicate debits/dispatch. Subscription access and compute balance are separate gates. Cost-aware extraction: evaluate reliable text-layer extraction before spending GPU time, then OCR where justified. Must demonstrate preserved structure/symbols on the benchmark before becoming a default. Using a cheaper route is not itself a quality improvement. Engine alternatives are benchmark candidates, not automatic new dependencies or migrations. These are proposed improvements consistent with the user’s direction, not approved novelty claims or completed features. Each must justify saved setup or correction time. Integration means portable outputs usable in the user’s own tools; it does not require proprietary Obsidian/AI plugins.
Benchmark before differentiation claims Use permission-cleared documents covering a clean digital textbook, scanned/older print, multi-column paper, mathematical tables/formulas, phonetic symbols and long-book section boundaries. Keep private source books private; use original synthetic/openly licensed samples for public demonstrations and third-party uploads only where permitted.
For each: exact engine/version/options; selected pages; byte/page counts; output integrity; missing/duplicated sections; significant symbol/numeric errors; broken image references; reading-order failures; human correction minutes per sampled page; elapsed time and actual billed cost. Errors without U+FFFD remain possible. A source-map page count is not proof that all source content survived.
Compare the same documents/tasks with native MinerU output and appropriate existing converters. Provider capability descriptions establish candidate baselines, not local victories. Choose differentiation only when observed: lower total cleanup time, less setup, clearer price, or a better supported difficult-document profile. No need to invent a feature that no other tool has; measurable utility is the commercial test.
Commercial experiment: 20 qualified testers, at least 5 actual paying users and 3 second-month returns are initial decision checkpoints, not market-size estimates. Keep larger development/paid acquisition proportional to evidence. At $1/month, assess net contribution and owner support time; popularity alone is insufficient.
