description: Editing modes, keyboard controls, safe previews, exports and draft boundaries.
text:
Open a text note or choose Take a note…. Checklists keep their separate checklist editor.
Write, Preview and Split change the view without discarding source or enhanced-editor undo. Split stacks vertically on narrow screens. Standard keys work by default. Vim enables normal/insert/visual modes, motions, selection and Vim undo. Use i to insert, Escape to return to normal, v to select and u to undo. Escape in Vim stays inside the note. Simple text provides a native textarea for accessibility, device compatibility or enhanced-editor loading failure. Switching to/from it starts fresh enhanced-editor undo; source is retained. Settings apply to this editing session. Undo, Redo, Find and the formatting buttons work in the enhanced editor. Find includes replacement. Tab leaves the editor instead of trapping keyboard focus. Save or Ctrl/Cmd-S writes through the normal API. Vim :w uses the same path. Existing notes stay open after these saves; Save & close also closes. Saving a new note completes its creation. Escape/backdrop closure asks before discarding an edited note; it does not silently save it. A failed save leaves the draft and undo available. If another tab changed the note, copy or download the draft before Reload saved version. Reloading is a deliberate replacement and clears the old draft’s undo history. There is no durable server revision archive yet. Download .md exports the exact current body, including unsaved changes, with the title as a portable filename. It does not insert a heading or modify stored data. Account JSON export still includes all notes and labels. Privacy and limits Markdown rendering, syntax and Vim run in the browser. No AI request, external font or paid processing provider is added. Preview supports CommonMark and GFM tables/task lists. Raw HTML is ignored. Only explicit HTTP(S), mail and fragment links are clickable; application-relative and script/data/file links are disabled. External links open separately without a referrer. Images display their description and an optional external link, never an automatic image request.
Source text remains in the existing note body; no database migration is needed. The enhanced editor preserves whitespace and mixed line separators by using explicit LF splitting. Its 100,000 UTF-16-unit limit matches the existing API boundary. An oversized paste is rejected whole, with a visible message, rather than silently truncated. Account-wide quotas and request limits still apply.
Drafts and undo exist only in the open tab. Save before navigating, and keep downloads/backups for important material. A tab-close warning is not crash recovery. Neither content nor editor preferences are copied into localStorage. This is not end-to-end encryption.
Public example /example uses the same editor with original demonstration text. It needs no account and sends no scratchpad to an API. Its Ctrl/Cmd-S and Vim :w download Markdown. Reset and ordinary navigation warn before discarding changed content. This is a scratchpad demonstration, not simulated cloud persistence.
Implementation MarkdownEditor owns views, fallback, status and download; CodeEditor owns one CodeMirror instance with replaceable key/read-only compartments. Callbacks route through the current component state; the global Vim Ex command routes through a WeakMap keyed by actual editor instance. Component cleanup destroys the view and removes its save handler. Switching views/keys retains history; a deliberate saved-version reload remounts it.
Both enhanced editing and Markdown preview load in separate client chunks. A failed editor chunk falls back to the controlled native textarea, preserving text. A failed preview chunk leaves Write available. The dependency set is pinned in the lockfile; CodeMirror, its Vim adapter, react-markdown and remark-gfm are MIT licensed. No raw-HTML plugin or weakened script CSP is used.
Primary references: CodeMirror state/view documentation , official Vim adapter , react-markdown security , remark-gfm . Installed Next 16.3.8 client/lazy-loading guides were read for this implementation.
Automated browser evidence is Chromium on Linux. Physical mobile keyboards, IME composition, screen readers and Safari/Firefox remain separate compatibility checks; the native textarea is available without pretending those devices have been certified.

description: Recognition, review, file retention, cost controls and the boundaries between outputs.
text:
Amir explicitly made the transcript product active ahead of Keep, delegated a stronger brand and asked for hosted ASR/LLM processing, Paddle and a Pageweft-like usage model. Sonaweft is the selected brand (bounded exact-name searches found no obvious matching software listing; this is not trademark clearance). Preserve instascript imports/command and existing remote URLs. Noteweld is the proposed next Keep brand; its implementation remains deferred.
Source decisions: CLI-001/002/003/005/009/010/013/022/023/033/037/041 and the current chat. Broad audiences and good defaults; English first; user-authorized media; Linux CLI/self-hosting plus hosted UI. Success: ingest media, hear/read timestamped ASR, keep original text, save separate corrections, optionally derive a faithful summary/research questions, export Markdown/JSON/SRT/VTT and a versioned bundle. AI review must not silently change the source or pretend to verify facts. A selected all-or-none hosted package is charged only after all its deliverables complete; retained private ASR checkpoints support explicit retry.
Release choices Host FastAPI and bounded workers on the existing owner Modal account, with separate Sonaweft volumes, secrets, ledger and Paddle product/prices. CPU/GPU scale to zero. Retained storage, scheduled cleanup, API calls and checks remain usage, not a guaranteed $0 bill. Speech: faster-whisper 1.2.1, pinned PyAV 15.1.0, SYSTRAN’s MIT large-v3 conversion on an on-demand GPU. Local CLI keeps CPU/int8 and can reuse existing small weights. Large weights are not installed on the laptop. Optional LLM: verified existing DeepSeek credential; official available IDs deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro (GET models returned 200). Separate standard/advanced choice, explicit transcript-sharing consent, bounded input/output and no automatic paid retries. Provider credentials stay out of browser/storage exports. Groq remains a cheaper ASR candidate ($0.04/h turbo, $0.111/h full Whisper in current docs) but no Groq credential/account is present; no fictional integration is enabled. Payments: one-time USD $5/$10 processing packs, no recurring access fee. Tariff: $0.15/job + $0.015 per started minute; optional standard review adds $0.10 + $0.005/minute, advanced adds $0.20 + $0.01/minute. This is a service price, not exact provider reimbursement or proven net profit. A 60-minute recording costs $1.05 transcription, $1.45 with standard review or $1.85 advanced before pack sales tax. Actual measured costs still need comparison. Bounded trial: first 30 seconds, transcription only, once per workspace/IP hash, at most three globally per UTC day and twenty per UTC month, additionally subject to admission/storage caps. Free use is never unlimited; no $0.50-per-IP guarantee. Uploaded source/result retention 48 hours; financial/recovery records persist separately. At most five retained uploads per workspace, 512 MiB source storage globally to start, two active jobs per workspace; initial file/duration limits are displayed by the deployed configuration. Owner estimated admission caps: $1/day and $2/month, including failed attempts. These do not cap the entire Modal/provider bill. Preserve immutable ASR; edits have revisions and cannot overwrite another session silently. The shared instascript-export/v1 schema carries stable segment IDs, timing, provenance, hashes and separately marked corrections/review. A failed import should later be atomic in Noteweld; its importer is not implemented by producing an export. Browser Vim and Obsidian-style editing belong to Noteweld: CodeMirror Markdown/Vim, app navigation separately opt-in, wiki links/backlinks, tags/themes, bounded local graph, lexical search and portable vault export. No proprietary Obsidian runtime or arbitrary shell/Neovim process is embedded. Evidence and limits Baseline: 11 dependency-light tests passed. An actual local ASR probe found Nix library-path requirements and PyAV 19 incompatibility (metadata_errors removed); the pinned release corrects the latter. Subsequent evidence belongs in RELEASE.md, not in unsupported quality claims. No application can promise perfect speech recognition, universal platform URL access, verified truth or guaranteed income. Paid access remains gated by the real seller/domain approvals and isolated payment tests described in OPERATIONS.md.

description: Stable note identities, title resolution, graph controls and connection limits.
text:
Choose Link note while writing to insert a stable reference such as [[note:UUID|Readable caption]]. Search titles/labels, select a note and insert; the editor keeps your cursor position and undo. Escape closes the picker and returns focus. A stable ID survives a rename; its optional caption remains the text you wrote, while the link tooltip shows the current title. Copy a stable reference from any note’s detail page too.
You can also type [[Title]] or [[Title|caption]]. Matching uses trimmed, case-folded NFKC titles across your own active and archived notes. Exactly one match resolves. Duplicate titles show ambiguous; missing titles show unavailable. These are name lookups, not permanent identity: use the picker for links that must survive renames or replacement by another note with the same title. Empty titles cannot be looked up by name; link them by ID. No note is created or rewritten automatically.
Wiki references must fit on one line, with at most 200 characters in each target/caption. Escape brackets, pipes or backslashes with a backslash; the picker does this. Code blocks, inline code, raw HTML and existing Markdown links/images (including GFM autolinks) are excluded. Syntax scanning is shared by the preview, metadata, backlinks and graph. The first 256 valid references in a note participate; a visible notice explains when more remain literal source. Downloads/account exports retain the full source.
Reading and backlinks Internal preview links open /dashboard/note/ID. These authenticated detail pages show full Markdown or a checklist, note controls, copyable stable references, outgoing links and saved backlinks. Archived notes still work. Trash is excluded from the connection index; a trashed reference becomes unavailable and works again after restoration. Permanent deletion never retargets a stable reference, including when another note gets the same title. Guessed IDs from another account return a generic not-found result.
In an open note, expand Links and backlinks. Outgoing references use the current draft, while backlinks come from saved notes. Repeated references from the same source do not create extra backlinks. Existing labels serve as tags and graph filters. They retain their current ownership, rename and deletion behavior.
Connections refresh after confirmed writes in the same workspace. Use Refresh connections, Refresh graph, or the header refresh to see other-tab changes. This is snapshot data, not live collaboration. Ordinary internal-link navigation warns before discarding an unsaved draft. A failed navigation does not clear the draft guard; a failed detail refresh retains the previous note. Header refresh also checks for unsaved work. Browser history/navigation and crash recovery are not a durable draft system: save important changes first.
Graph Open Graph in navigation. It includes active/archived notes and excludes Trash. Filter titles or labels, choose one label, include/exclude archive, or focus a note and its immediate neighbours. Filters intersect; Reset filters returns the whole view. Fit graph frames the actual visible positions, including small graphs, and adapts to viewport size. Labels/dots retain a readable screen size while zooming. Camera buttons work with keyboard or touch; mouse dragging pans the background. The HTML note list and native focus selector provide equivalent navigation without requiring SVG interaction.
There is no continuous physics loop, animation tracking or network polling. A deterministic bounded layout is computed when graph data/filters change. At most 500 nodes and 1,000 directed edges are drawn; the current free account quota is still 250 notes. The node-limit control and an explicit warning disclose truncation. A reference beyond a note’s 256-reference limit is not counted as an edge/backlink; reduce or split that note to include it. Self-links remain valid but do not add graph edges or self-backlinks.
Try the same renderer without an account at /example/graph . Its six original notes are fixtures, with local anchor navigation; it reads no private API or cloud account and does not pretend to save user notes.
Implementation and operations /api/knowledge authenticates before database access, selects only the owner’s non-trashed rows and returns minimal derived metadata, not note bodies, account identifiers or credentials. Label ownership is checked too. The existing no-store/nosniff/CSP boundaries remain. Parsing uses pinned MIT-licensed mdast-util-from-markdown, mdast-util-gfm and micromark-extension-gfm, already shared with the Markdown toolchain. No HTML execution or wider image/network policy is added.
Metadata is fetched lazily when needed and kept only in the open workspace. Versioned/abortable requests reject stale responses; confirmed writes invalidate the snapshot. The route is bounded to 500 notes, with 30 requests/minute per account and 120/minute globally. Per-account admission happens before global admission so a single throttled account cannot consume the entire global counter. Fixed-window boundary bursts and provider-wide spending controls are not universal load/abuse certification.
No schema migration, original Keep database access, payment change, new provider or always-on service is required. Rollback to the Markdown/Vim release preserves bodies and ordinary account functionality; wiki syntax becomes text there. Source-bundle imports must later map imported identities explicitly rather than reusing another account’s IDs.
Primary parser references: from-markdown , GFM AST extensions , GFM syntax extensions . Installed package APIs and Next 16.3.8 client/route/lazy-loading guides were read before implementation. Current test/publication evidence belongs in connection release ; Firefox/Safari, physical touch/IME and formal accessibility certification remain separate checks.

description: Browser, isolated ledger, media handling, speech workers and payment events.
text:
Browser --> secure cookie + CSRF --> FastAPI / Modal |--> serialized SQLite ledger writer |--> private media volume (48-hour TTL) |--> confirmed CPU coordinator |--> FFmpeg normalization |--> L4 / faster-whisper large-v3 |--> optional DeepSeek text review |--> committed result --> settle hold Review player / separate corrections / portable exports <--| Explicit selected claim --> Crossref metadata candidates Isolated checkout --> Paddle --> signed durable inbox |--> fresh transaction + all adjustment pages |--> intent/owner/product-bound credit or revocation instascript/contract.py validates original ASR and exact source-quoted review and creates versioned exports. pipeline.py provides local private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication. review.py bounds text/output, validates JSON and has no autonomous tools. Local source.py downloads are never invoked for public uploads.
sonaweft_web/app.py handles ownership, CSRF, request limits, consent, quotes, revisions, exports and isolated checkout. media.py restricts FFmpeg to file/pipe protocols and rejects network-capable playlist formats. storage.py validates UUID paths and audio byte ranges. Aggregate activity logs exclude transcripts and filenames.
Ledger confirmation atomically reserves fixed credit and estimated admission allowance before dispatch. Repeated request IDs reserve once. Success consumes the complete quote; failure/cancellation/stale timeout releases it. Cleanup releases work exceeding the 20-minute deadline; a late worker cannot settle a released hold. No automatic paid retry is made.
Signed notification payloads cannot fund accounts alone. Fresh Paddle transaction/adjustment verification checks server-owned intents, owner, product/prices, quantity, currency and environment. Refund revocation is monotonic; queued work is cancelled if necessary and debt blocks new work. Running work may finish with negative available credit while the invariant remains checked. Unknown transactions/products are ignored. Mocks do not establish real delivery or approval.
Separate media/model/ledger volumes isolate state. Hourly cleanup deletes expired files and retains seven daily encrypted financial snapshots with media metadata removed. Session-key rotation invalidates sessions/IP hashes; old keys are needed for old cloud snapshots. Owner-downloaded backups use a separate generated key.
One speech container/coordinator and bounded uploads, rate limits, trial/admission/storage caps limit initial exposure. Estimated admission caps are not provider-wide hard spending limits. Storage, requests, failed work and schedules can still cost money.
Sonaweft and Pageweft share reviewed owned payment logic and currently an account-scoped Paddle runtime key, with distinct product/prices, notification secret, sessions, ledgers and volumes. They have no sibling runtime imports or shared customer wallet. Key rotation affects both until separate keys are configured.
Future Noteweld imports must validate schema, size, paths, hashes and duplicate identity before one atomic import. Stable segment IDs/provenance preserve the original/corrections/notes distinction. Exporting a manifest does not implement that importer.
Legacy summarize/LLM adapters, Claude/UTCP examples and vault scaffolding are compatibility/history paths, not the hosted pipeline. Jev is retired. Research metadata matches never certify truth.
title: Processing architecture

description: CPU hosting, isolated PostgreSQL, encrypted snapshots and incident recovery.
text:
Scope and least privilege The hosted preview uses a new database and login role on the existing Neon project, separate from the old Keep database. The original credential files and original two accounts are preserved. Migration credentials remain private on the owner’s machine; only the new runtime role is sent to Modal. It has connection/schema-usage/table CRUD privileges, no database/schema creation or role-management privileges. All app queries enforce ownership; PostgreSQL RLS is not claimed.
The Modal app/secret/backup volume are noteweld, noteweld-runtime, noteweld-backups-v1. AUTH_SECRET is unique to this app. It is not a Sonaweft/Pageweft shared login or wallet. There is one CPU web container, maximum 20 concurrent inputs, 3 database connections, 1536 MiB RAM, no GPU and no always-on minimum. Cold starts are expected. Neon compute can suspend, but retained storage, maintenance and real provider usage are not a universal $0 billing guarantee. Provider-wide hard spending caps/automatic external alerts have not been verified.
Signup is capped at 100 total accounts and 50 new attempts/day; IP and account login/recovery throttles live in PostgreSQL. Trusted proxy handling uses the final forwarded address, and global caps remain even if that header cannot be trusted. Quotas count trash too; restore does not bypass them. There is no polling or advertising/third-party analytics script. Logs return generic errors and omit request contents; provider access logs have separate retention.
Owner actions Create a project operations venv with python -m venv .venv-operations and install requirements-operations.txt; authenticate your own Modal profile. Never send connection URLs, keys, recovery secrets or dumps to chat/Git.
.venv-operations/bin/python scripts/owner.py report .venv-operations/bin/python scripts/owner.py maintain .venv-operations/bin/python scripts/owner.py backup --output .local/backups/noteweld-NEW.fernet Reports show aggregate counts only. Maintenance removes counters older than two days and writes an encrypted daily backup, retaining seven daily files. This also runs at 02:23 UTC daily. Encryption uses an independent BACKUP_KEY stored in the provider secret; securely save a separate owner copy. Losing the key makes backups unreadable. No public admin/backup endpoint exists. Manually downloaded backups need owner-controlled retention; do not leave them indefinitely.
For incidents: stop new access by stopping the Modal app in the authenticated dashboard, inspect aggregate logs and Neon availability privately, fix/redeploy, then verify health/login and restore access. No user content is needed in logs. Cookie resets/recovery revoke all prior sessions by database sessionVersion. Deletion cascades through notes/labels; live reads then reject old cookies. Existing unrelated provider apps are not stopped.
Deployment and rollback Pin reviewed source and run unit/lint/types, isolated migrations/database/browser checks and build. Inspect outgoing Git diff for secrets. Never execute automatic migrations against the old Keep database. For a fresh isolated database, migrate with an explicit privileged DATABASE_URL in the process environment; grant the restricted runtime role usage and CRUD on that new database’s public schema/tables. Retain migration access locally. For an existing database, first take a backup and audit case-folded email/label collisions. Migration 0002 intentionally fails on duplicates; resolve ownership explicitly instead of auto-merging accounts. Create noteweld-runtime from a private JSON file with DATABASE_URL, AUTH_SECRET, AUTH_URL and AUTH_TRUST_HOST=true; BACKUP_KEY is also required by owner backup/maintenance functions. Use modal secret create ... --from-json PRIVATE_PATH; use --force only to update that same app’s reviewed values. Preserve AUTH_SECRET and BACKUP_KEY during routine releases. Deploy with python -m modal deploy app.py. Record the actual returned hostname, update AUTH_URL to that exact HTTPS origin and redeploy. Use a private immutable staging copy if editing source while the remote build runs. The app image allowlists files and cannot include local credential files. Verify /api/health, production CSP, no-cache responses and an actual synthetic account/create/reload/recovery/delete journey on the returned URL. Then update portfolio links. Billing stays closed. Code rollback: deploy the preceding reviewed source with the same new database/secret. Do not blindly reverse migrations or point the preview at the original Keep database. For a data incident, restore a backup to a new empty database, verify it, then update only this app’s DATABASE_URL and redeploy. Keep the damaged database intact for investigation until recovery is confirmed. Restore on a new target Decrypt the Fernet snapshot locally using the separately stored BACKUP_KEY, writing a mode-0600 temporary file in a private directory. The hosted pre-OAuth release emits format=noteweld-backup, version 1. The account branch emits version 2 with OAuth identities; the updated restore accepts both versions into an empty target migrated through 0005. The snapshot includes account password/recovery hashes and private note text; never print it. scripts/backup-format.mjs verifies table/column names, locks all five persistent app tables, including oauth_identity, in the updated account source and refuses any non-empty target.
Create a new empty PostgreSQL database, apply this source’s migrations with privileged access, and set NOTEWELD_RESTORE_DATABASE_URL to that exact target using private environment handling. Run:
node scripts/restore.mjs PRIVATE_DECRYPTED_FILE EXACT_NEW_DATABASE_NAME Compare counts, representative note/checklist content, labels and login/recovery in the clone before a cutover. Delete the temporary plaintext file after the check. The automated local test restores actual synthetic records into a fresh temporary database and confirms a second restore cannot overwrite it. This does not justify restoring into the old live Keep database. Neon provider recovery retention is separate from these seven-day application backups.
Primary/installed references Installed Next 16.3.8: node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/content-security-policy.md, proxy/error conventions and 03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/output.md. Drizzle transactions , Neon role access . Modal web servers , image builds , secrets , volumes . description: Usage reporting, admission controls, pause, encrypted ledger backups and recovery.
text:
Run from the Pageweft repository with the existing authenticated Modal profile. There is no publicly accessible admin endpoint or new monitoring subscription.
.venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations report .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations pause .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations resume .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations budgets --daily 10 --monthly 25 .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations backup .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations verify-backup .local/operations/backups/ACTUAL-FILENAME.fernet report writes private .local/operations/dashboard.html and JSON. Open the HTML locally. Refreshing means rerunning the command; this is a generated snapshot, not a live stream. It retrieves the actual current-cycle Modal workspace billing summary through the installed SDK and displays it separately from internal estimates. Missing provider data is reported as unavailable, never assumed zero. Aggregate activity includes bots/reloads; it does not prove unique users, conversion rates or causal attribution. Recognized landing tags: ?utm_source=portfolio, github, obsidian or research; arbitrary values collapse to other.
Admission and pause controls Defaults: $10/day and $25/UTC calendar month of admission envelopes, separate from the customer’s processing tariff. Each <=20-page GPU attempt consumes $0.15 of this envelope; text-only consumes $0.01. Every new attempt, including explicit retries and free samples, is admitted atomically before dispatch. Credit reservation, page quotas and admission all roll back on rejection. Duplicate confirmation does not consume another envelope. Failed and cancelled work does not recycle envelopes. Existing legacy attempts before this release are not retrospectively counted in the new budget.
These amounts are provisional safety allowances, not measured invoices or an absolute cloud-cost ceiling. GPU workers cap two cores/8 GiB, timeout 240 seconds and scale down after five seconds; body timing still excludes cold load/idle. HTTP, parser, ledger, coordinator, cache, storage, egress, private owner extraction scripts and pre-existing workloads are outside the admission envelope. Work can cross day/month boundaries. Shared startup costs make per-section attribution approximate. Do not promise a $25 maximum Modal bill from this control.
Pause rejects new confirmations/retries, preserves retained exports and checks queued sections before GPU dispatch. Already dispatched/running work can finish and charge its successful pages. Queued sections encountered by the coordinator are cancelled and their customer holds released. Inspect pending sections after pausing; never assume every running container stopped.
The platform’s independent outer control is Modal Usage & Billing , reached through the authenticated dashboard if the path changes. According to Modal budgets documentation , workspace usage budgets cover the whole workspace and workspace spend limits cap net out-of-pocket charges after applicable credits; environment budgets require Team/Enterprise. The installed 1.5.3 SDK exposes billing reads but no documented budget/spend-limit setter. No provider-level spend limit has been configured or verified by this release. Set an owner-approved net limit in the actual dashboard and verify the displayed saved value; this also affects Linguavell preparation/private extraction in the same workspace. Do not upgrade to the $250 Team plan merely for environment budgeting.
Money: four different quantities Pack face value is customer-funded service allowance, not profit. Available plus reserved positive credit is an undelivered obligation; negative credit after a refund is debt, not income. Consumed service is cumulative and survives job/file cleanup. The ledger checks funding − revoked = available + reserved + consumed. Pure verified-live accounts are separated from fixture/unverified/mixed accounts. Actual cash contribution requires receipts after processor/payout fees/refunds, plus actual attributable compute and other expenses. Monthly actuals are deliberately entered from statements, not inferred from tariffs. .venv/bin/python -m scripts.operations actuals --month 2026-10 --net-receipts 0 --modal-cost 0 --other-cost 0 This syntax example is not an instruction to record unverified zeros. Enter actual totals; net-receipts is service receipts after refunds/processor/payout fees, excluding customer sales tax. modal-cost should match the documented allocation of the bill; distinguish cash billed after credits from underlying metered cost when judging long-term tariffs. Include acquisition, support and other attributable cash expenses in other-cost. Cash difference is not distributable profit: outstanding credits, tax, owner labour and timing still matter. Keep provider statements privately with the row’s basis.
Monitoring and incident handling The existing hourly cleanup also reconciles up to 50 least-recently-checked live orders, makes a daily encrypted financial snapshot and emits sanitized operational alerts into Modal logs. At larger order counts reconciliation latency grows: inspect the provider’s signed refunds promptly and deliberately increase/replace the bounded batch before expansion. It skips payment API calls while live billing is unconfigured. Failure to reconcile is counted and logged without order payloads. No email/Slack alerts or messages have been activated. On Starter, platform log retention is limited; persistent aggregate metrics survive separately.
Pause and investigate when credit invariants fail, costs exceed recorded receipts, at least three section failures exceed 20%, or repeated server/payment errors occur. Inspect owner dashboard → platform function logs → affected private job/receipt, without posting customer data in public GitHub issues. At 80% of an admission budget, inspect traffic and actual bills before increasing a cap. A spend limit that stops the whole workspace can also stop cleanup; purge expired files after service resumes.
HTTP protections include scoped encrypted sessions, CSRF/origin checks, ownership enforcement, 64 KiB JSON bounds, bounded upload size, hashed-address rate quotas and global quota ceilings. PDF inspection runs in a child process with 15 CPU seconds, 20-second wall timeout and 768 MiB address-space limit; parser errors are sanitized. These are hardening measures, not an independent penetration test or a guarantee against every denial-of-service attack. Initial quotas can reject legitimate shared-IP users; paid growth requires deliberate calibration.
Backup and restore The serialized writer creates consistent SQLite snapshots. Snapshots remove correction text/history, source filenames/digests and vacuum discarded pages; no PDFs or output ZIPs are backed up. Accounts, purchase/grant/revocation records, credit holds and operational aggregates remain. Cloud snapshots are encrypted with the existing session secret, stored privately for seven daily versions and require that key to restore. Off-laptop copies of the key are needed; losing the key and all backups prevents recovery.
Owner backup instead encrypts a snapshot with an independent local .local/operations/backup-key.fernet and checks decryption, SQLite integrity and credit identities on a disposable clone. Keep the encrypted file and key separately off this laptop. Never upload a key to Git or paste it in chat. This verification does not overwrite production or prove a disaster cutover. A financial backup does not restore expired documents or edits.
For actual disaster recovery: pause web/dispatch; stop the existing writer; decrypt into an isolated file; verify integrity and credit identities; restore into the same volume with the sole writer stopped; redeploy one writer; reconcile queued/running holds and authoritative provider refunds; check two isolated sessions and an owner report before resuming. Do not start another app writing the same SQLite volume, delete live volumes, or blindly replace newer credit transactions with an older snapshot. Routine code rollback preserves the additive schema and the permanent session secret; the pre-operations source/database backup is retained privately.
Sources retrieved 14 October 2026: Modal billing CLI , pricing and billable load/idle , workspace spending controls , Lemon Squeezy order/refund fields . No account approval or billing limit is inferred from documentation.

The operations JSON includes pending/stale payment-event counts, with an alert for delays beyond five minutes. Other seller products without a Pageweft checkout intent are ignored. Fresh transaction/adjustment reads enforce ownership and refund totals. Original record: Book conversion release — 14 October 2026.
Implemented in the hosted Pageweft application; supersedes the one-page-only product and $1/month access proposal. Amir delegated a better pricing model and approved the conversion utility improvements. The public free sample remains one selected page, but inspection accepts books and paid jobs use separately funded credits.
Features and implementation Capability Implementation Books / ranges / batch inspection Up to five PDFs, each <=64 MiB and 1,000 source PDF pages; strict PDF validation and page-range parser; retained inspected PDFs can be resumed. Each conversion is separately confirmed. Preview and price before extraction Source page count, selected pages and text-layer samples are inspected without GPU work; fixed tariff quote must match the confirmation. Automatic / force OCR / cheaper text-only Pinned unmodified MinerU 2.7.6 uses its documented mode/language options; pypdf text-only worker uses no GPU and explicitly excludes OCR, image extraction and layout reconstruction. Bounded sections / partial recovery Selected pages split into groups of 20; at most two GPU workers. Successful sections survive failures; explicit retries select missing or chosen original pages and can force OCR. Duplicate requests cannot reserve or dispatch twice. Traceability / fidelity review Original page indices are mapped from the subset PDF back to the full source. Renderer preserves recognized headings, equations, HTML tables, captions, footnotes and images. Unhandled blocks, unmapped content, empty/short output, missing images and replacement glyphs are reported. Untouched engine output is retained separately; flags do not certify correctness. Corrections / history Plain Markdown editor with original-PDF page link, optimistic edit versions and saved history. Reprocessing retains user corrections. Engine text can be loaded explicitly into the editor draft. Portable outputs Single Markdown, individual pages, bounded page groups, or sections based on original PDF bookmarks. Local image paths, source hash, unavailable-page list, raw section extraction and review metadata. Source PDF inclusion is optional. Cancel / discard / delete / expiry Queued work releases reserved allowance. A running cancelled section may finish and be charged. Job deletion removes edits/output and releases an unshared source. Unused inspected sources can be discarded. Hourly cleanup removes 48-hour-expired files; balances/recovery persist separately. Account / purchase recovery Encrypted Secure/HttpOnly session; high-entropy recovery key stored only as keyed hash. One-time purchase keys can restore the owning account. No customer Modal credentials. Payments / refunds Separate one-time pack integration verifies scoped provider orders and signed events; duplicate orders grant once, full/partial refunds revoke pack credits. Atomic reserve/settle/release accounting in integer 1/10,000 USD units. Public test-mode grants disabled. Live seller configuration remains absent. The active HTTP factory is web/studio.py. web/main.py and web/billing.py preserve the retired interface/verifier for regression/compatibility work; they are not the public paid implementation. Books use /ledger/books.sqlite, separate from the original /ledger/state.sqlite. Each is owned by one serialized function. Do not run a second Modal app with a separate book_store function on the same volume. Owner verification scripts invoke deployed functions instead.
Pricing No recurring access fee. One-time $5/$10 processing packs; the service debit is:
MinerU: $0.50 service fee plus $0.005 per selected page. 100 pages = $1; 500 pages = $3; 1,000 pages = $5.50. Text layer only: $0.25 plus $0.001 per page. 500 pages = $0.75. This is a cheaper, explicitly more limited extraction route. Reprocessing already completed pages: $0.20 service fee plus the chosen method’s page rate. Failed-page retries do not repeat an already charged initial service fee. Failed sections release their page allowance. If no section succeeds, the service fee is released too. Existing successful work and its charges remain. These are launch service tariffs, not exact pass-through of a measured Modal invoice. Credits do not expire; files/edits do. Prepaid funds are not all profit when purchased. Taxes may be added at checkout; fees/support/refunds/compute reduce contribution. Recalibrate tariffs from representative actual bills before expanding spending limits.
Lemon Squeezy fees : base 5% + $0.50, additional 0.5% for subscriptions, possible international/PayPal charges and non-US payout fees. The main savings here come from avoiding monthly microtransactions and amortizing the fixed checkout cost over prepaid use. At a simplified base fee, $5 leaves $4.25 before payout; $10 leaves $9. International and tax effects can reduce this further.
Modal pricing : A10 $0.000306/sec, CPU $0.0000131/core/sec, RAM $0.00000222/GiB/sec. New GPU sections request/cap two CPU cores and 8 GiB RAM, with 240-second function timeout, 180-second extraction bound and 5-second scale-down window. Model load, waiting, storage and orchestration can add cost. This is not invoice measurement or a guarantee every PDF finishes within the bound.
Initial safety limits: 100 retained-document creations/day globally; five retained inspected documents per owner; GPU page attempts 3,000/day globally and 2,000/owner/day, text attempts 30,000/day globally and 5,000/owner/day. Failed attempts still count toward safety limits, despite credit refunds. Trial capped at 3/day and 20/month globally, once per owner/IP. Shared-IP restrictions can affect legitimate users. These caps protect initial owner spending and must be deliberately calibrated for growth; no thousands-of-concurrent-user capacity claim is made.
Owner operations addition The private owner report now retrieves actual Modal workspace billing, separates verified commercial funding from fixtures, retains cumulative service consumption across file cleanup and checks credit identities. Atomic admission envelopes default to $10/day and $25/UTC month, at $0.15/GPU or $0.01/text section attempt. These are provisional controls, not a provider invoice cap. Pause blocks new/queued dispatch with an explicit allowance release; running work may complete. Rate quotas, 64 KiB JSON bounds and a separate CPU/memory/time-bounded PDF inspector harden the HTTP path. Read OPERATIONS.md and LAUNCH.md for the outer provider spending limit and actual payment/account/customer evidence.
Existing hourly cleanup adds bounded refund reconciliation, encrypted financial snapshots without document text/filenames, and sanitized rule-based alerts. Off-platform financial backup decryption/integrity/credit identities are checked on a disposable clone, not by overwriting production. No email alert or third-party analytics service was connected. An original public PDF/Markdown/ZIP guide and crawl metadata are available; indexing and sales are not established.
Evidence Automated suite: 60 unique checks, including real 1,000-page PDF inspection/end-section extraction, timeout/funds lifecycle, actual PDF-bookmark exports, refund cancellation, retry replay and malformed-request tests. Real Modal MinerU: original four-page PDF, selected pages 1/3/4, produced mapped portable output. This was an owner-authenticated internal credit fixture, not a purchase. Real deployed CPU: the complete original 1,000-page synthetic PDF processed across 50 sections via deployed book_store/run_book functions, with fixture credit and no second ledger writer. Final archive has all 1,000 ordered source pages, zero unavailable pages and the correct $1.25 service-credit debit. Four-page source selection was also checked. This is text-layer extraction of a synthetic PDF, not a scanned-book or technical-fidelity benchmark, and not a customer payment. Real public HTTP: inspection of pages 3–4, unfunded confirmation rejected with 409, one-page sample delivered original page 3, edit saved, corrected per-page ZIP downloaded with source PDF omitted, other session denied. Local Chromium: real PDF text extraction and explicit local seeded credit at widths 320/390/768/1440; quote, confirmation, correction history, selective reprocessing and ZIP download passed; no horizontal overflow/page errors. Batch inspection checked at 320/1440. Browser fixture does not verify payments or local GPU extraction. Actual seller checkout, provider test-mode webhook delivery, funds arrival, payout and a representative difficult-book comparison are not verified. No claim of perfect OCR, fixed damaged IPA or superior extraction is made. Ignored artifacts contain sanitized evidence/synthetic PDFs; source books and secrets are not added. Screenshots and browser errors are private test artifacts. No new local AI model was installed and no NixOS configuration was changed.
